newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds strong after U.S. labor cost index.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds strong after U.S. labor cost index.

text.p: Argentine bonds were much higher in busy late morning activity Tuesday, benefitting from a surge in U.S. Treasuries following a lower-than-expected fourth-quarter employment cost index.
"The market reacted very well, it is rising strongly," said a trader at a foreign bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.40 to 125.70, while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 surged 3/4 to 89-1/2.
The U.S. fourth-quarter employment cost index rose 0.8 percent, lower than analyst expectations of a 0.9 percent rise.

Analysts at MMS International said in an investor note: "Brady bonds are strengthening on the friendly ECI data and the strength of U.S. Treasuries." The 30-year U.S. bond yield was last nine basis points lower at 6.85 percent.
Another trader said he expected the strong performance to continue through the session considering the fact that U.S. Treasuries recovered from their losing streak of recent days.
